title: Boolean Matrix Rank via Monomial Ideals

title: Adjoints of Morphisms of Neural Codes
relationship: Question 7.1 repeats and extends the canonical-form extremal problem to union-complete codes; Conjecture 7.3 gives the same redundancy/rank equality. Predates the dissertation.
evidence_locator: v1, 11 March 2026; Sections 7.1 and 7.3, Question 7.1 and Conjecture 7.3

title: Cohomological support varieties under local homomorphisms
relationship: Dissertation-related restriction-of-scalars and finite-flat-dimension results. No resolution of the proposed nonflat derived extension established by this search.

title: Cohomological support varieties for monomial ideals
relationship: Extends a monomial-ideal classification and reports answering a Gintz question. That named question is not the nonflat-extension direction in our Watson review.

title: Graded-Injective Modules and Bass Numbers of Veronese Submodules
relationship: An article version of the Bass-number work, not evidence that the answered dissertation Question 1 remains open.

relationship: Linear Stokes/elasticity result and FEM consequences. Does not claim global well-posedness of the full untruncated nonlinear FSI problem.
evidence_locator: Abstract; first posted 10 November 2025, revised 23 January 2026

title: Point Prediction for Streaming Data
relationship: Core streaming-prediction work. Consistency is under IID hypotheses; this is not model-free consistency for every M-open stream.

title: Online Prediction for Streaming Observational Data
relationship: Survey of prediction methods for observational/M-open streams. Relevant continuing research; no specific turnstile-extension theorem verified here.

title: Absorbing sets in quantum LDPC codes
relationship: Peer-reviewed publication of absorbing-set/decoder research; received April 2025 and revised January 2026. Publication after the thesis is not by itself new progress on its future-work questions.

relationship: Topic-matched conference paper listed by the author. Full theorem comparison was not available from the accessible IEEE landing page.

title: Combinatorial Analysis of Dyadic and Quasi-Dyadic Codes
relationship: Cites Martinez–Pllaha–Kelley as reference 22. Remark 3.4 explicitly describes Theorem 3.1 as a partial converse of that paper’s Theorem 4.6 and conjectures the full converse. Sections 4.1 and 4.3 develop walk/cycle correspondences and girth extensions. This is concrete later progress on the research family, not a verified resolution of every graph-lift direction.
evidence_locator: v1, 3 May 2026; Theorem 3.1, Remark 3.4, Section 4.1, Theorem 4.19, Remark 4.2, reference 22

relationship: Later preprint claims exact dynamic programming for a different changepoint framework. Its exactness theorem is not a proof of convergence or global optimality of the older IRFL iterates.

title: Interpolation in Weighted Projective Spaces

title: On the algebraic properties of the Böröczky configuration
relationship: Later weighted-projective-plane application to ideal generators and symbolic-power containment. Does not establish uniform boundedness of the general defect or weighted Horace.

title: Sandwich Bernstein-Sato Polynomials and Bernstein’s Inequality
relationship: Gives a criterion for Bernstein’s inequality and sandwich-equation existence in specified settings, with a Segre application. The introduction expressly notes failure for general singularities. The audit’s broad question must be read as a classification of valid settings, not a conjecture affirming every ring.

title: Calmed 3D Navier-Stokes Equations: Global Well-Posedness, Energy Identities, Global Attractors, and Convergence
relationship: Published calmed-NSE work; a global attractor for a rotational calmed NSE is a different target from the calmed velocity–vorticity attractor question.
evidence_locator: Abstract; Journal of Nonlinear Science 34 (2024), 112; DOI 10.1007/s00332-024-10093-9

title: Algebraic calming for the 2D Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equations
relationship: Global well-posedness of the calmed approximation and convergence on the original solution’s existence interval; not global well-posedness of the original 2D equation.

title: Calmed Ohmic Heating for the 2D Magnetohydrodynamic-Boussinesq System: Global Well-posedness and Convergence
relationship: Post-thesis application of calming to 2D MHD-B with Ohmic heating. Different dimension/equations from the original 3D MHD target; convergence assumes original solutions exist.
